 Nicholls, Phillips rally New Zealand after Bumrah burst 
 Unbeaten centurion Henry Nicholls added a 173-run stand with Glenn Phillips that lifted New Zealand from 70/5 to 243/5 against India in Wellington.
 19 November, 2026 New Zealand v India scorecard 
 After a stellar Test ton, Henry Nicholls called a Test against India at the Basin Reserve “a special occasion” at the post-game press conference.
 Earlier, Nicholls had spent majority of the opening day of their First  World Test Championship Test notching up an unbeaten 113* that rescued New Zealand from a precarious position after India struck early in the day.
 View this post on Instagram 
 “Test cricket has always been the pinnacle for me,” Nicholls said after play.
 “We love playing Test cricket, and you play at a venue like this, and against a team like India, it’s a special occasion.”

 The left-hander credited the build-up to the Test for his composure against the moving ball.
  “We came here early, and I certainly think the training we had out here made me feel really prepared,” he said.
 “We know when we come to the Basin (Reserve) that it’s going to be a challenge if you lose a toss and get put in.”
 View this post on Instagram 
 That challenge arrived in the morning, when India captain Shubman Gill won the toss and bowled first on a green pitch, and Bumrah made the decision look inspired from the third ball of the match, nipping one back through Tom Latham’s shouldered arms to clip the off-bail for a duck. 
 Anshul Kamboj had Devon Conway caught behind by Rishabh Pant for 4, Akash Deep found the edge of Rachin Ravindra (15) for another Pant catch, and Bumrah returned to have Daryl Mitchell caught at short leg by Yashasvi Jaiswal for 1 after Gill brought a close fielder into play. New Zealand went to lunch at 60/4, and Bumrah removed Tom Blundell soon after the break to leave the hosts stranded at 70/5.
 “India bowled fantastically well in the morning session and we were under some pressure,” Nicholls said.
 He highlighted Jasprit Bumrah as the main strike-bowler for India, as he claimed three wickets in the first two sessions, including the Kiwi skipper Tom Latham in the first over of the Test.
 “Jasprit Bumrah is Jasprit Bumrah, so we know the challenges that he offers any time he plays. Incredible bowling.”
 Jasprit Bumrah: Journey to the Top
 Bumrah's early scalps meant Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips were at the crease with a tough job on their hands, however the duo persevered.
 The pair’s approach was built on simple reminders.
 “We were just trying to remind each other to control what we can control,” he said. 
 “If they’re going to bowl well, make them have to keep bowling well throughout the day.”
 On batting with Phillips, he added, “Anytime you play with someone who’s looking to put that much pressure on the bowler, sometimes it can make your job a little bit easier. He’s great to bat with.”
 What followed was a lesson in absorbing pressure and then returning it. Nicholls, unbeaten on 29 at lunch, held firm while Phillips took the attack to the bowlers.
 Nicholls completed his hundred in the 70th over with a single off Prasidh Krishna, finishing the first day on 113 from 221 balls, his fifth Test century at the Basin Reserve in just 15 innings there.
 Glenn Phillips, who struck his maiden Test hundred at The Oval in June this year, was 94 not out from 182 balls, six short of a second Test century at the conclusion of Day one.
 View this post on Instagram 
 In the India camp, coach Sitanshu Kotak felt that while pacers held the sway early, the sunshine meant the pitch dried out faster. 
  “It was a sunny day, so probably it dried out quicker than even the curator would have thought, but that nobody can control,” he said.
  “I feel that in new ball we are getting more help, after 30 overs or 35 overs even the seam of the Kookaburra ball is a little tight. So after that, the way they batted, credit to them.”
 Kotak also pointed to where India could have been better.
 “Maybe we could have bowled a little more on the stumps to Phillips, because he got a lot of runs on the off side,” he said.
 There was a chance late in the day, after Nicholls pulled a ball that went straight to Devdutt Padikkal, but the fielder dropped it.  
 He admitted, too, that India had let a chance go during the stand. “It was a mix-up,” Kotak said. “We still should have caught it.”
 However, Kotak was complementary of India's pace maverick, Jasprit Bumrah, highlighting his skill and how he could be one the younger bowlers learn from.
 “He is someone with unbelievable skills.”
 The paceman had been rotated through the day, he explained, because “he also needs that recovery time”, and he felt the younger bowlers in the attack could learn from him.
  “When you have a senior bowler like that, it’s definitely a lot of learning for other bowlers as well.”

 Jasprit Bumrah shined for India in the World Cup.
 On India’s attack, saw the absence of the experienced Mohammed Siraj, Kotak said selection was never about one day.
 “When you pick an 11, you think about all four or five days it will go on,” he said. “It is not just one day.”

 Mohammed Siraj has broken Australia's massive partnership, claiming the wicket of Travis Head on Day 2 at The Oval.
 New Zealand are well aware that they needed to build on their excellent start before India's bowling strikes back on Day Two. 
 "As many (runs) as we can get, to be honest,” Nicholls said of a target to set for India in the second innings.
 “The Indian guys will be fresh again in the morning. The start of any day, let alone with a new ball, is always a challenge.”

 First Test : 19-23 November, Wellington
